newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African chemical, oil sector wage talks deadlock.
newsitem.headline: S.African chemical, oil sector wage talks deadlock.

text.p: Wage talks in South Africa's strategic chemicals and oil industry are deadlocked over pay, working hours and maternity leave, employers said on Thursday.

Oil industry labour spokesman Simon Drysdale told Reuters the Chemical Workers Industrial Union (CWIU) had applied on June 26 to the Council for Conciliation, Mediation and Arbitration (CCMA) to intervene and a hearing was likely in two weeks.
The industry has offered a 9.5 percent wage increase and workers are demanding 14.5 percent, Drysdale said.
"On hours of work, they are looking for 40 (hours per week) with no loss of pay. Currently the sector as a whole is on 42, excluding Sasol," he said.
"I hope that we can resolve it at the CCMA but I am not too optimistic... At this stage every single sector in the chemical industry is in deadlock, it is not only petroleum.
The workers' demands were in line with Congress of South Afrian Trade Unions objections levelled at the proposed Basic Conditions of Employment Bill.
Drysdale said that the oil industry was probably the highest paying in South Africa.

"We have agreed to a 2,000 rand minimum wage for the sector, but, for example, BP (South Africa) are paying a 2,800 rand a month basic wage with an overall package of over 5,000 rand, including housing and all the other benefits," he said.
